messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a short design decision to align Python/TS/Go SDKs on transport & retry semantics for paginated endpoints. High level problem: users expect resumable pagination + sensible retries without surprising duplicate side effects.

 tom: Agree. Current gap: Python returns async iterator that retries transparently; TS exposes pageToken and requires manual resume. Go has a streaming callback pattern. In practice this confuses customers.

 kyle: Proposal: define a canonical mapping from API surface (unary, streaming, paged) -> transport flavors (HTTP/gRPC) -> retry model (per-request idempotent vs per-page). That way SDKs implement the same user affordances.

 anya: Important callout: for non-idempotent mutating pages (rare but exists) we must never do automatic retries across page boundaries. Instead surface an explicit resume token + opt-in retry helper.

 maria: +1. Sketch of mapping: 
 - unary (single response): standard idempotency header + automatic retry w/ exp backoff
 - paged (cursor/token): default: retry only within single page fetch; preserve and surface last-seen cursor on retry failure; do not autop-retry page-fetch that might re-run server-side mutation without idempotency
 - streaming (server stream): best-effort reconnect with resume token if server supports it

 sam: Quick pseudo for TS ergonomic surface: 
 ```ts
 // default iterator
 for await (const item of client.listWidgets()) { /* ... */ }
 // opt-in strict resume
 const it = client.listWidgets({ resumeOnFailure: true });
 ```
 We should avoid leaking transport details to simple loops.

 kyle: For Go, keep the callback approach but add a small RetryPolicy param and an explicit ResumeAfter(token) helper. Example:
 ```go
 client.ListWidgets(ctx, opts, func(item *Widget) error {
   // user code
 })
 ```
 Plus opts.RetryPolicy = RetryPolicyResumeOnFailure

 anya: On timeouts: set conservative per-page deadline default (30s) and a shorter connect timeout. Allow per-call overrides. Document the cost/latency tradeoff.

 maria: What about error classification across transports? We need a canonical set: transient (TCP/reset, 5xx, 429), permanent (4xx other than 429), retryable-after (retry-after header) — SDKs should map transport-specific codes to this set.

 ops-bot: deploy-bot: New staging build with retry-telemetry enabled for experiments (build 2026.03.21.12)

 tom: Implementation plan: 
 1) finalize canonical mapping + examples (this thread)
 2) small RFC doc with table + migration notes
 3) prototypes in each SDK and opt-in flag
 4) dogfood with internal paging-heavy customers

 kyle: One more: telemetry. Each automatic retry should emit token-level metric: page_retry_count, resume_attempted boolean. Avoid PII in tokens.

 maria: Action items: I will write the RFC draft (short) by EOD Friday. Tom and Kyle will implement prototype flags. Anya to list known non-idempotent paged endpoints. Sam to review TS ergonomics.

 sam: ack :thumbsup:

 tom: ack

 anya: ack

 maria: thanks — keeping this lightweight will help us ship consistent behavior across SDKs without breaking existing users.
